HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives measures success within a 100-item candidate set, not full-catalog top-10 retrieval. Sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; fixed candidates ensure comparable trials but do not remove sampling bias. Interpret improvements strictly under the pinned benchmark, without changing its evaluator. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

For uncertainty, a suitable application of paired bootstrap is to resample users with replacement within each category, preserving each user’s baseline/proposal hit indicators and candidate set. Recompute the four-category macro-average difference for each replicate; report its 95% interval and category-level changes. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. This interval measures user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; it excludes training-seed and negative-sampling variability. [SciPy paired bootstrap](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html).

Repeated adaptive hyperparameter selection can overfit validation noise; an ordinary bootstrap interval for the selected winner does not correct that selection bias. Treat small gains as provisional until the host’s independent held-out evaluation. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html). Mathematically, positive score scaling or any strictly increasing transformation preserves ranks, hence HR@10, apart from numerical ties. Raw logit margins can therefore grow without ranking improvement. Diagnose actual positive ranks, hit/miss transitions, and the positive score relative to the tenth-highest negative; margin magnitude alone is scale-dependent. Temperature changes during training can alter learned rankings, unlike inference-only scaling.
